# returns/ (tax return versions)

Wave 5 L1a + L1b. One `tax_return_versions` row (mig 969) per finalised VAT201 or EMP201 for a period, plus the version chain an amendment builds; L1b (mig 971) adds file, amend and the one-open-draft index on `sars_submissions`.

## Caller contract
Called by `pages/api/accounting/sars/returns/[form]/{finalise,versions,file,amend}.ts`. Every function takes `companyId` first; `finaliseReturn` takes the actor's `{ userId, role }` from withAuth.

## Main signatures
- `finaliseReturn(companyId, form, periodStart, periodEnd, actor, { overrideReason?, force? })` -> `ReturnVersion`. `assertNotImpersonating` first (Login-as 403). One savepoint around everything, so a refusal leaves no lock, no `vat_gate_overrides` row and no version even though withAuth commits a 4xx. `ReturnRefusal` (400/409) is raised only before the first write.
- `listVersions(companyId, form, start, end)` -> `{ versions: (ReturnVersion & { drift, lockRemoved })[], vatReturn }`. Read-only.

- `markReturnFiled(companyId, form, versionId, reference, actor, overrideReason?)` -> `{ version, submission }` (`fileReturn.ts`). `assertNotImpersonating` first; owner/admin/super_admin only (403, same as amend); a reference with no visible character (whitespace, zero-width) 400; unknown id or wrong form 404; not `finalised` 409; a VAT201 whose lock was released outside the lifecycle 409; a version that has drifted (`driftOf`) 409 naming the fields (amend, finalise again); an EMP201 filing takes the company's payroll approval lock (`lockCompanyPayrollApprovals`) first, so the drift check and the commit see one payroll state. Then ONE savepoint: `saveDraftSubmission` with `keepExistingAs: 'pageDraft'` (form_data is ALWAYS the version's figures plus `returnVersionId`/`versionNo`, which the submission modal renders; a draft the page saved is kept under `pageDraft`; a draft with `efiling_correlation_id` set, an in-flight ISV submit, is 409), `assertVatGateClear(…, 'sars_submission', id, …)` (VAT201 only; owner/admin override with a reason), `markSubmitted(…, { lifecycle: true })`, the version's move to `filed` (`returnVersionWrites.markVersionFiled`) and an audit row (`logAuditOrThrow`, entity `tax_return_version`). A refusal leaves no submission, no override row, no version change. The routes are rate-limited per user (`return-file:u:`, `return-amend:u:`).
- `amendReturn(companyId, form, versionId, reason, actor)` -> the superseded `ReturnVersion` (`amendReturn.ts`). Owner/admin/super_admin only (403), a reason with a visible character mandatory (400), Login-as 403, audited. A VAT201 takes the VAT exclusive key, then the version row FOR UPDATE; ONE savepoint supersedes the version (`amended_*` stamps) and `unlockVatPeriod`s ONLY that version's own lock by id (skipped when it was already released; a replacement lock is never touched). The next finalise makes version N+1 (`amends_version_id` = N); its filing is a new submission.
- `assertLockNotInLiveVersion` (`liveVersionGuard.ts`) is called by `unlockVatPeriod` after it holds the lock row and before it writes: a lock named by a non-superseded version is 409 "amend the return" (`VatPeriodAmendRequired`). Amend supersedes first, so its own unlock passes.

## Business rules
- **Periods** (`returnPeriod.ts`, after `reportWindowProblem`): an EMP201 is exactly one ended calendar month (1st to last day, `periodEnd` before today SAST; a nil return for it is allowed). A VAT201 is one period of the company's cycle (`companies.vat_period` monthly or bi-monthly, `vat_period_alignment` odd/even end months, as `bureau/vatPeriodHelper`); a non-vendor is refused. Overlap with ANY live version of the form is 409 (`assertNoLiveOverlap`, re-run under the VAT key).
- A submitted `vat_returns` row with other figures is 409 unless the request carries `acknowledgeVatReturnMismatch: true` and `mismatchReason`, kept in `figures.meta.vatReturnMismatch`. The finalise response returns the record with its `mismatch` flag.
- Stored EMP201 figures carry `directiveTotals` only; `directivePayments` is always `[]` (one person's pay each).
- **Dead end, pinned:** a VAT version whose lock was unlocked directly through `/vat-period-locks` stays live (`lockRemoved`), so finalising again (or an overlapping period) is 409; `amendReturn` is the way out (a version whose lock was released directly can still be amended; it just has no lock to release). The unlock route now refuses a lock a live version names, so this state can no longer be made through the API. `lockVatPeriod`'s auto-snapshot is scheduled after its insert and may fire for a lock a refusal then rolls back.
- **VAT201** = `computeVatLockFigures` -> 15% check (`force` records it) -> `assertVatGateClear` (owner/admin override with a reason) -> `lockVatPeriod`. `created: false` is a 409 ("locked outside the lifecycle"). The version copies the LOCK ROW's figures; nothing is computed a second time. The sole guard against a pre-existing lock is `created`, not a pre-read.
- **EMP201** is refused (409) unless every non-cancelled run of the period is final by `isPayRunFinal` (FS's approval time: `approved`/`paid` with `COALESCE(approved_at, approval_grandfathered_at)` set; never a status string alone). `generateEMP201` still sums by status string, so the check is on its output: a summed run that is not final blocks. Headers are `FOR SHARE`d so a reopen waits. No payroll lock (decision 7). `posted_through` = latest `approved_at` among the summed runs.
- One non-superseded version per (company, form, period): finalising again is 409. The next version (after an amend, L1b) links `amends_version_id` to the newest one.
- Drift = regenerate and compare: VAT output/input/net and `sarsFields`; EMP PAYE, ETI, payable, UIF, SDL, employees, taxable remuneration, directive totals, the run set with each `approved_plan_hash` (`changed: ['runs']`) and `unfinalRuns` (a summed run no longer R-035 final). `lockRemoved` = the version's lock has `unlocked_at` (someone used `/vat-period-locks` directly). `vatReturn` is the older `vat_returns` row, shown with a mismatch flag; this module never posts and never writes it.
- Writers: 969 revokes INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER from app_user, app_service, platform_admin and PUBLIC (352's default privileges gave platform_admin UPDATE/DELETE); app_user keeps SELECT and column INSERT (no `status`: rows are born `finalised`). An ENABLE ALWAYS trigger refuses every DELETE and any UPDATE of the recorded figures, period, chain, lock or `finalised_*` for every role, owner included (L1b widens it for status/filed/amend). A BEFORE TRUNCATE statement trigger refuses TRUNCATE (it skips row triggers and RLS); 969 sweeps UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE from every grantee but the owner and migration_admin (952's aclexplode loop). A BEFORE INSERT trigger refuses another company's submission, an amend of another form/period, and a lock that is not this company's ACTIVE lock for the same period. Tests that must fake a moved ledger lift it with `withVersionsMutable`.

## Rollback (read before rolling back after versions exist)
`scripts/rollback-deploy.sh` is code only. The 969/971 triggers stay in the database when the old colour runs, and they refuse what the old code does for a period that has a version: a legacy or ISV mark-submitted (`sars_submissions_lifecycle_only`), re-marking a filed submission (`sars_submissions_filed_frozen`), unlocking a lock a live version names (`vat_period_locks_in_return`), and any UPDATE of `tax_return_versions` by the old code (none exists there). Periods WITHOUT a version behave as before. If a rollback must also let the old code file or unlock such periods, Hein runs these as the table owner, knowing they remove the guard:
`DROP TRIGGER trg_sars_submissions_lifecycle_only ON sars_submissions;`
`DROP TRIGGER trg_sars_submissions_filed_frozen ON sars_submissions;`
`DROP TRIGGER trg_vat_period_locks_in_return ON vat_period_locks;`
(`trg_tax_return_versions_immutable` and `trg_tax_return_versions_same_company` stay: they only constrain the new code.) Re-create them from `971_tax_return_file_amend.sql` when rolling forward.

## DB rules added by 971 (the L1b carry-overs from the #1248 reviews)
- app_user may UPDATE exactly `status, sars_submission_id, filed_reference, filed_by, filed_at, amended_*` (column grants, never table-level); the 969 sweep still holds for every other role and 971 ends with a postcondition on both levels.
- `sars_submissions` has NO unique index for one open draft and no dedupe in 971 (the old colour of a blue/green deploy and a code-only rollback INSERT drafts plainly: an index would make that 23505 for as long as it runs). `saveDraftSubmission` takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on (company, form, period) and a row lock on the latest open draft. The index plus a dedupe of existing duplicate drafts ship in a follow-up migration after the next deploy.
- `markSubmitted` (legacy route) refuses (409, `SubmissionNotOpenError`) a submission that is not a draft, one a version names, and any draft of a period that has a return version of ANY status (the amend gap: nothing live, still the lifecycle's; unless `lifecycle`). The ISV path (`submitVAT201ToSars`) refuses the same periods before anything outbound (`versionExists.periodHasReturnVersion`). Triggers back it: `sars_submissions_lifecycle_only` (draft to submitted for a period with any version needs the transaction-local flag `app.return_lifecycle`, which only `markReturnFiled` sets: defence against application bugs and the old colour of a deploy, not against SQL-capable app_user, who can set it), `sars_submissions_filed_frozen` (status, reference, submitted_at of a named submission, every role) and `vat_period_locks_in_return` (no unlock of a lock a live version names, every role). Tests that fake a lock released outside the lifecycle use `releaseLockDirectly` (trigger off in one transaction).
- Stamps: `filed_by`/`amended_by` must equal the sub of `request.jwt.claims` (withAuth) and `filed_at`/`amended_at` be within five minutes of the clock; direct SQL with no session user cannot file or supersede. This guards against application bugs, NOT against a SQL-capable app_user, who can set its own claims: only REVOKE holds there. The amend stamps change only with the move to superseded. Reference and reason need a visible character (`returnGuards.visibleText`; the SAME set, including U+00AD, U+034F, U+061C, U+FFF9-FFFB, U+13430-1343F, U+1BCA0-1BCA3, U+1D173-1D17A, U+115F-1160, U+17B4-17B5, U+180B-180F, U+2000-200F, U+2028-202F, U+205F-206F, U+2800, U+3164, U+FE00-FE0F, U+FEFF, U+FFA0 and the tag block, in the trigger).
- `tax_return_versions_immutable` guards transitions for every role, owner included: finalised to filed or superseded, filed to superseded, nothing out of superseded (a superseded row is frozen); filing stamps are set together, only by the move to filed, once only; a move to filed needs a submission and a reference; a move to superseded needs the amend stamps.
- `tax_return_versions_same_company` fires BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF `sars_submission_id, amends_version_id, vat_period_lock_id` and judges a reference only when it changed; the submission must be this company's, for this form and period, and `submitted`.
- A period already filed the legacy way (an unnamed `submitted`/`accepted` submission overlapping it) makes the lifecycle filing a 409 `LEGACY_SUBMISSION_EXISTS` naming it, unless the request sends `correctsLegacySubmissionId` (that row's id) and a visible `reason`: the legacy rows are then marked `superseded` in the same savepoint (flag on) and the audit row names them. ANY change to a non-draft row of a period with a version needs the lifecycle flag. A NUL in a reference or reason is a 400. The ISV path takes the period's draft advisory lock, re-reads, and commits its intent event in its own transaction (`insertEfilingEventCommitted`: an ordinary app_user connection from the withAuth pool with the request's claims and company GUCs, never a migration credential) before anything goes to SARS.
- A submission-less or stamp-less `filed` row cannot exist; tests that must fake a moved ledger still lift the trigger with `withVersionsMutable`.
